findings.title: Meditation programs and psychological stress (meta-analysis of trials)
findings.evidence: meditation programs can result in small to moderate reductions of multiple negative dimensions of psychological stress.

findings.title: Meditation/mindfulness and anxiety, depression (NIH summary)
findings.evidence: The analysis included more than 12,000 participants, and the researchers found that for treating anxiety and depression, mindfulness-based approaches were better than no treatment at all, and they worked as well as the evidence-based therapies.

findings.title: Meditation and blood pressure (NIH summary)
findings.evidence: According to a 2017 statement from the American Heart Association, the practice of meditation may have a possible benefit, but its specific effects on blood pressure have not been determined.

findings.title: Religion/spirituality and health: research review (scope)
findings.evidence: followed by a review of relationships between R/S and heart disease, hypertension, cerebrovascular disease, Alzheimer's disease and dementia, immune functions, endocrine functions, cancer, overall mortality, physical disability, pain, and somatic symptoms.

note: These findings are mostly observational associations (people who do a practice vs. people who do not), which cannot show cause and effect; trial evidence exists mainly for meditation programs, with small to moderate effects. Mosaic Bond makes no claims about supernatural effects and does not score faith. Practice tracking here is neutral and private.
